title: Ascletis’ challenger to Lilly’s Foundayo hits goals in phase 2 diabetes trial
summary: A phase 2 trial of Ascletis’ oral GLP-1 drug candidate has hit its primary and secondary endpoints, positioning the Chinese biotech to mount a two-front attack on Eli Lilly’s Foundayo.

title: Genmab's $8B Merus bet delivers as bispecific combo halves risk of death in phase 3
summary: Capping off a busy few days in Spain, Genmab reported results from the first interim analysis of a phase 3 trial showing that adding its bispecific antibody petosemtamab to Merck & Co.'s Keytruda cut the risk of death by 50% compared with Keytruda alone in patients with PD-L1-positive recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.

title: FDA’s rare disease framework aims to ‘stand the test of time’
summary: During a public hearing Wednesday to discuss a newly proposed rare disease framework, FDA center director Michael Davis, M.D., Ph.D., said the agency aims to design a scheme that “stands the test of time.”

title: Biogen CEO tells analysts he’s focused on early-stage R&D as ‘we were not very good with that’
summary: Biogen's CEO has pointed to the company's ability to take five drugs into clinical trials so far this year as evidence of its new focus on early-stage R&D.

title: ‘The patient need is enormous’: Syntax programs stem cells into pancreatic beta cells in 4 days
summary: Chicago-based Syntax Bio believes it has cracked the code for turning stem cells into pancreatic beta cells in as little as four days.

title: Lilly’s retatrutide bests Ozempic on blood sugar, weight loss in phase 3 diabetes showdown
summary: Eli Lilly’s triple-G drug candidate retatrutide has beaten Novo’s Ozempic in a head-to-head phase 3 trial, driving deeper reductions in blood sugar and body weight across the 80-week study.

title: GSK predicts ‘some limited impact’ to UK roles as restructuring rolls on
summary: GSK’s global restructuring plan is likely to see “some limited impact” to roles on the Big Pharma’s home turf of the U.K., executives have confirmed.

title: Astellas makes $1.3B bet on Audax’s preclinical push to reverse decades of IL-12 woes
summary: Astellas has struck a deal for Audax Biosciences’ IL-12 program, committing up to $285 million in upfront and option fees to secure a chance to license the preclinical immuno-oncology program.

title: Artiva lays off 94% of staff after deaths and durability sink autoimmune cell therapy
summary: Artiva Biotherapeutics has halted development of an autoimmune disease cell therapy and laid off 94% of its staff after two patients died and durability data fell short of expectations.

title: From RAS rivalries to leaked cancer vaccine readouts, ESMO brought the data drama
summary: Every ESMO conference is eventful, but the drama kicked into gear earlier than expected this year when the eagerly anticipated phase 3 data for Moderna and Merck & Co.’s cancer vaccine were leaked two days before the Presidential Symposium.

title: Parkinson’s-focused Aspen and bispecific biotech Bambusa both shoot for $134M IPOs
summary: Parkinson’s disease cell therapy-focused Aspen Neuroscience and bispecific biotech Bambusa Therapeutics are each hoping to raise around $134 million from their respective IPOs.

title: Corxel claims oral obesity drug is in the ‘right lane’ as biotech plans SPAC route to Nasdaq
summary: Corxel Pharmaceuticals may not have always planned to dust off the SPAC route to the public markets, but the obesity-focused biotech is happy with its choice.

title: Labcorp continues acquisition spree as it buys up Millennium Health
summary: Labcorp is acquiring Millennium Health to boost the medtech giant’s toxicology testing capabilities throughout the U.S.

title: BMS joins 3-year partnership to boost participation in cancer trials
summary: The Institute for Healthcare Improvement has partnered with Bristol Myers Squibb on an initiative to expand access to cancer trials.

title: Novartis CEO keeps faith in Avidity deal despite taking $1.9B hit from del-desiran fail
summary: Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan has insisted that the phase 3 fail for del-desiran is just a “bump” in the Swiss pharma’s wider plans for the drug, despite costing the company an estimated $1.9 billion.

title: GSK’s B7-H3 ADC drives 67% cancer risk reduction in Hansoh's phase 3 China trial
summary: A phase 3 trial has linked GSK’s risvutatug rezetecan to a 67% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death, providing evidence that B7-H3-directed antibody-drug conjugates work in relapsed osteosarcoma.

title: Boehringer, Microsoft team up to explore digital patient twins for clinical trials
summary: Boehringer Ingelheim and Microsoft have launched a collaboration to explore the use of AI-powered digital patient twins to improve clinical trial design.

title: Anthropic lays out drug R&D ambitions, risks in mammoth IPO filing
summary: Artificial intelligence giant Anthropic is pushing deeper into drug discovery, building its own molecular biology lab and investing in research that could eventually produce drug candidates, according to the company's blockbuster IPO filing.

title: Lycia leaps onto Nasdaq with upsized $318M IPO as Windward breezes toward listing
summary: Lycia Therapeutics went public with an upsized $317.5 million IPO on Friday, while immunology-focused Windward Bio is hoping to catch the same tailwinds.

title: ESMO: Why Incyte sees itself ‘neck and neck’ with RevMed in KRAS G12D pancreatic cancer race
summary: Incyte has pointed to a spread of phase 1 data for its KRAS G12D inhibitor as evidence that the company has a worthy rival to Revolution Medicines in this increasingly competitive cancer space.

title: BioNTech sees ‘limited’ benefit to ADC after phase 3 reveals modest efficacy, ILD cases
summary: BioNTech has reported modest efficacy and unexpected safety findings in a phase 3 breast cancer trial, leading the company to conclude its HER2-directed candidate may offer limited benefits in the current treatment landscape.

title: BMS sheds light on patient death in CAR-T trial, wants to get program back on track
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb has shared more details with Fierce about the death of a patient who received the pharma's investigational CAR-T in a multiple sclerosis trial.

title: ESMO: Genmab posts phase 3 win for Elahere rival, ahead of ‘very interesting’ data from Merus buyout
summary: Genmab may have arrived in Spain with updated data from a pair of phase 2 studies from the main prize of its Merus buyout, but the company had bigger news to share.

Why Some People Love Hugs While Others Hate Them
summary: Why do some hugs stay with us while others fade away? A survey of more than 15,000 UK adults published in PLOS One shows that 70% remember hugs for comfort, with empathy, relationship attachment styles, and body perception dictating how touch is stored in memory.

title: Nearly Half of Distressed Adults Use AI for Therapy
summary: Are chatbots becoming informal therapists? A new study reveals that nearly half of adults experiencing severe psychological distress turn to generative AI tools for emotional support, raising urgent questions about clinical safety.

title: Breathing “Thin Air” May Protect Against Parkinson’s
summary: Can breathing thin mountain air help Parkinson's patients? Researchers demonstrated that 39 minutes of controlled intermittent hypoxia safely lowers stress hormones, raises anti-inflammatory adiponectin, and protects BDNF levels without disturbing sleep.

title: Developing Fetal Brain Weeds Out Genetically Flawed Neurons
summary: Why does the prenatal brain overproduce millions of neurons only to eliminate them? A landmark Nature study led by Harvard Medical School and Boston Children’s Hospital shows that the developing brain uses competitive synaptic pruning to weed out neurons carrying abnormal DNA mutations.

title: Brain Scans Fail to Predict How Well Individuals Regulate Emotions
summary: A 2,175-person study led by CIMH reveals prefrontal cortex activation does not reflect how well an individual regulates emotions via cognitive reappraisal.

title: CTE Affected 75% of Deceased NFL Veterans
summary: How common is CTE among professional football players? A new study corrects for brain donation selection bias, estimating that 74.5% of all NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 had chronic traumatic encephalopathy.

title: Finding the Brain’s Mood Switch in Bipolar Disorder
summary: What causes the sudden transition between depression and mania in bipolar disorder? Researchers at USC, Stanford, and Johns Hopkins received a $4.5M BD² grant to study "retrosplenial switch cells"—a unique neuronal population that may control mood switching.

title: How Ego and Self-Image Change Brain Sync
summary: Why do some individuals struggle with genuine empathy? Brain scans show that people with high grandiose traits fail to synchronize their brain activity with others when watching someone lose face or experience social vulnerability.

title: Walking Speed Sharpens Visual Sensitivity to Backward Motion
summary: Why is the brain extra sensitive to backward motion while walking? Research shows that at typical walking speeds, our visual system detects smaller speed changes in contracting optic flow, functioning as a vital reflex to prevent backward falls.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, Visual Neuroscience, backwards motion, brain research, National Institute of Natural Sciences, neurobiology, visual neuroscience, walking

title: Why the Left Brain Controls the Right Body
summary: Why does the left side of your brain control the right side of your body? Neuroscientists at the University of Minnesota propose that the brain’s cross-wiring originated from the optical inversion of ancient eyes, which forced motor and sensory circuits to follow a contralateral map over 500 million years ago.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, brain research, evolution, evolutionary neuroscience, Fontiers, movement, neurobiology, optic chiasm, visual neuroscience

title: Wearable Vagus Nerve Devices Rewire Depressive Brains
summary: Vagus nerve stimulation is a proven treatment for depression, but it has historically required surgery. A comprehensive review in Med-X shows how wearable ear and neck bioelectronics are transforming non-invasive VNS into an accessible, AI-guided home therapy.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, Psychology, brain research, brain stimulation, depression, mental health, neurobiology, Neurotech, vagus nerve, vagus nerve stimulation

title: Brain Stimulation Stops Sexual Objectification
summary: Sexualized images of women are often processed visually like objects rather than people. A new study shows that 10 minutes of non-invasive brain stimulation restores holistic human recognition, temporarily erasing this objectification bias.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, brain research, brain stimulation, neurobiology, Neurotech, objectification, sexual objectification, tDCS, University of Exeter

title: Serotonin signaling enhances phagocytosis by brain macrophages through Htr2b and alleviates brain injury after stroke
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02482-yThe serotonin receptor Htr2b activation enhances lysosome biogenesis and phagocytic clearance of debris to mitigate neuroinflammation and brain injury after stroke. The study proposes a potential monocyte-derived macrophage-targeted immune therapy to improve neurological outcomes after ischemic stroke.

title: Stimulus-specific recruitment of human amygdala neurons predicts episodic memory encoding success
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 27 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02493-9The study shows that stimulus-specific neurons in the human amygdala determine which experiences become lasting memory, revealing a mechanism that predicts episodic memory formation and may guide future treatments for memory disorders.

title: Circuit mechanisms for disentangled representations and generalization in the hippocampus
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 27 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02491-xThe hippocampus encodes different aspects of experience as disentangled variables, enabling flexible recombination and generalization to new situations. This code is supported by the geometry of population dynamics and cell–assembly interactions.

title: Chronic progressive demyelination induces a microglial state with lysosomal dysfunction
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02489-5Acute myelin injury responses are well defined, but microglia adaptations to chronic damage remain unclear. Mouse models reveal a chronic demyelination-associated microglial state marked by inflammation, lysosomal dysfunction and myelin-damaging activity.

title: Microglial NUS1 deficiency drives dopaminergic neurodegeneration through intercellular iron dysregulation in Parkinson’s disease models
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02499-3Using cellular and mouse models, this study reports that deficiency of the Parkinson’s disease risk gene NUS1 in microglia disrupts intercellular iron homeostasis, leading to neuronal iron overload and dopaminergic neurodegeneration.

title: Identification of candidate markers for the isolation of neuron-specific extracellular vesicles
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02466-yThe authors developed methods to identify extracellular vesicles (EVs) in the blood that come from the brain by capturing EV surface proteins. This could be used in the future to diagnose neurological diseases.

title: Sustained antidepressant-like effects of psychedelics through 5-HT2AR–β-arrestin signaling
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02497-5This study shows that the sustained antidepressant-like effect of psychedelics is driven by 5-HT2A receptor–β-arrestin signaling. Repeated low-dose LSD preserves this effect in mice without inducing hallucinogenic-like behaviors in mice or monkeys.
